trigger: crop damage, hailstorm, flood, drought, unseasonal rain, pest attack, harvest loss, kisan, fasal bima, PMFBY, 72 hours, krishi

steps.text: Call toll-free helpline 14447 within 72 hours of localised event to get SMS ticket number
steps.source: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana Guidelines (pmfby.gov.in)

steps.text: Upload geotagged crop loss photos via Crop Insurance App or submit to Bank/CSC/Agriculture Officer
Surveyor must be appointed within 48 hours of intimation to assess loss

rule_note: Localised calamities (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst, lightning fire) and post-harvest loss (within 14 days) strictly require individual intimation within 72 hours. Widespread/area-wide yield loss uses area approach without individual intimation.

category: Free Legal Aid Eligibility (s.12 LSA Act)
trigger: free lawyer, legal aid, poor citizen, cannot afford lawyer, women legal help, SC ST legal aid, NALSA, DLSA, Tele-Law, section 12

steps.text: Check eligibility under Section 12 Legal Services Authorities Act (Women, Children, SC/ST, custody, disabled, disaster victims have no income cap)
Book free video/phone consultation with panel advocate via CSC or Tele-Law portal/app
Call NALSA 24/7 toll-free helpline 15100 or visit local District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) office

rule_note: First 7 categories under Section 12 have NO income eligibility test. For general low-income applicants, state-prescribed limit applies (typically up to Rs 3 lakh/yr depending on state).

trigger: unpaid invoice, MSME payment delay, buyer not paying, 45 days overdue, Udyam registered, 3x bank rate interest, vendor dues, IT service invoice

steps.text: Send formal statutory demand notice citing Section 15 & 16 of MSMED Act and Section 43B(h) IT Act
File delayed payment reference on MSME ODR / Samadhaan Portal with Udyam number and invoice proofs
steps.source: Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC)

steps.text: MSEFC conciliation / arbitration hearing with statutory compound interest with monthly rests at 3x RBI bank rate

rule_note: Applies strictly to Micro and Small suppliers with valid Udyam registration (Medium enterprises generally excluded). Maximum agreed payment period cannot exceed 45 days (15 days if no written agreement). Compound interest with monthly rests at 3x RBI bank rate is mandatory.

trigger: bank dispute, failed ATM, unauthorized transaction, UPI deduction, loan overcharge, credit card fraud, bank manager refused, account frozen, RBI ombudsman

steps.text: Submit written grievance to Branch Manager / Principal Nodal Officer of the bank and get acknowledgement
If 30 days lapse without resolution or complaint is rejected/unsatisfactory, escalate to RBI Integrated Ombudsman
File appeal with Appellate Authority under RBI Scheme within 30 days of Ombudsman award/decision if dissatisfied

rule_note: Pre-flight mandatory: Complaint must be made in writing to the bank first. User must wait 30 days unless bank rejects earlier. Limitation: Must file within 1 year of bank's final reply (or 1 year 30 days if no reply). No upper cap on compensation amount for financial loss.

trigger: defective product, fake goods, refund denied, e-commerce scam, hotel overcharge, flight cancellation refund, warranty dishonoured, misleading ad

steps.text: Send written notice / grievance to merchant / service provider and log complaint on National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915)
Determine jurisdiction based strictly on consideration paid (District Commission: up to Rs 50 lakh; State: Rs 50L - 2 Cr; National: > Rs 2 Cr)
File formal online petition through e-Daakhil portal or physical Commission registry

rule_note: Pecuniary jurisdiction is measured STRICTLY by value of consideration paid (not compensation claimed): District <= Rs 50 Lakh, State Rs 50L - 2 Cr, National > Rs 2 Cr. Limitation period is 2 years from cause of action.

trigger: police refused FIR, police station not registering complaint, cognizable offence, zero FIR, theft report refused, SP complaint, magistrate 175, BNSS

steps.text: Demand registration of FIR under BNSS s.173 (or Zero FIR at any station for cognizable crime) and get free copy s.173(2)
If officer-in-charge refuses, send written substance of complaint by registered post to Superintendent of Police (SP / DCP) under BNSS s.173(4)
If SP takes no action, file application before Judicial Magistrate under BNSS s.175(3) with affidavit of previous efforts

rule_note: Under BNSS s.173 (replaced CrPC 154 from 1 July 2024), police must record cognizable complaint. Preliminary inquiry up to 14 days allowed for offenses punishable by 3-7 years. Out of scope: bail, defense, or guilt advice.

trigger: talk to advocate, human legal review, legal aid clinic, court advice, free advice session, Nyaya Bandhu, pro bono advocate

steps.text: Book video/audio consultation with panel lawyer through Common Service Centre (CSC) or Tele-Law App
steps.source: Department of Justice, Govt of India

steps.text: Apply for assignment of a pro bono panel advocate via Nyaya Bandhu mobile app
Visit local Taluk/District Legal Services Authority front office for free counsel representation in court

rule_note: Strictly no private lawyer marketplace, directory or commercial advertisement per BCI Rule 36. Connects only to official Govt Tele-Law and DLSA/NALSA panels.

trigger: health insurance claim rejected, motor insurance delay, life insurance policy dispute, cashless rejected, IRDAI, Bima Bharosa, insurance ombudsman

steps.text: File formal complaint with Insurance Company Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO)
steps.source: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations

steps.text: Escalate to IRDAI Bima Bharosa portal (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in) or call 155255
Approach Insurance Ombudsman if claim remains unsettled after 30 days (claims up to Rs 50 lakh)

rule_note: Needs official re-verification before final submission. Bima Bharosa handles IRDAI escalations; Insurance Ombudsman handles personal claims up to Rs 50 Lakh.

trigger: sim blocked without reason, broadband bill overcharge, mobile portability rejected, MNP dispute, telecom operator grievance, TRAI

steps.text: Lodge complaint with Telecom Service Provider customer care and obtain complaint docket number
Escalate to Appellate Authority of the respective service provider with docket number
Lodge grievance on Department of Telecommunications (DoT) portal / CPGRAMS

rule_note: Needs official re-verification. Note: TRAI does not directly handle individual subscriber disputes; complaints go to TSP Appellate Authority or consumer forums.

trigger: cyber fraud, phishing scam, credit card hacked, money debited online, OTP fraud, fake telegram investment, 1930 helpline, cybercrime

steps.text: Immediately dial National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 to freeze fraudulent bank transfers in the golden hour
steps.source: Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System

steps.text: Lodge official online complaint on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in)
Submit acknowledgement with copy of complaint to bank branch within 3 days for zero liability review under RBI circular
steps.source: RBI Limiting Liability of Customers Circular

rule_note: Needs official re-verification. Golden hour reporting to 1930 enables immediate lien-marking on suspicious beneficiary accounts.

trigger: salary unpaid, employer not paying salary, wrongful termination, gratuity withheld, provident fund PF rejected, labour court

steps.text: Send written notice of salary demand to employer management
steps.source: Payment of Wages Act / Code on Wages

steps.text: File complaint with Labour Commissioner / Conciliation Officer of the jurisdiction
steps.forum: Office of Labour Commissioner / SAMADHAN Portal

steps.text: Approach Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal for claim recovery if conciliation fails

rule_note: Needs state-specific re-verification. Distinctions apply between workmen (covered under Industrial Disputes) and managerial roles (civil remedy/negotiation).

trigger: landlord refusing security deposit, illegal eviction notice, flat deposit refund, rent dispute, tenant harassment, rent authority

steps.text: Send formal legal notice to landlord demanding refund of security deposit with proof of handover
steps.source: Model Tenancy Act / State Rent Control Act

steps.text: File petition before Rent Authority / Rent Court of the respective district

rule_note: Needs state-specific re-verification. Tenancy laws vary by state (e.g., Delhi Rent Control Act, Maharashtra Rent Control Act, Model Tenancy Act implementations).

trigger: passport delay, ration card officer bribe, municipality garbage issue, pension delay, government office no response, CPGRAMS

steps.text: Lodge grievance on Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (pgportal.gov.in)
If unsatisfied with resolution, file appeal on CPGRAMS within 30 days to Appellate Authority

rule_note: Needs official re-verification. CPGRAMS does not handle court matters, RTI matters, or religious matters.

category: Other / Low Confidence / Legal Aid Handoff
trigger: general legal question, unknown issue, ambiguous grievance, defamation, divorce, property partition, boundary dispute

steps.text: This grievance cannot be automatically routed to a standard online ombudsman portal. Safe human review is recommended.
Call NALSA toll-free helpline 15100 or visit tele-law.in for guided human legal consultation.

rule_note: When confidence is below 60% or outside verified ombudsman scope, Haq Saathi does not guess. It safely routes to human legal aid.
